but whoever wishes to be greater among you shall be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave,
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his soul as a ransom for many.
But you seek to grow from what is small, and to grow [?] from what is lesser. When you go in and are invited to a supper, do not sit down
at once in the highest places, lest perhaps someone more distinguished than you comes, and the one who invited you to the supper comes to you and says to you: Sit lower down,

and then you will be ashamed. But if you sit down in the last place and someone humbler than you comes, the one who invited you to the supper says to you: Sit higher up, and then it will be more honorable for you.
And as they were going out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him. And behold, two blind men were sitting there by the way;
they heard that Jesus was passing by there, and they cried out, saying: Lord, have mercy on us, son of David. The crowd
rebuked them so that they would be silent, and they cried out all the more, saying: Lord, have mercy on us, son
of David. And Jesus stopped and called them, and said: What do you want me to do for you? They said:
Lord, that our eyes may be opened. Jesus had mercy on them, touched their eyes, and at once they saw and followed him. And when they drew near
to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two of the disciples, and said to them:
[?] they perceived that he was speaking about them, and they sought to seize him. They feared the crowds, because they held him to be a prophet.
And Jesus answered them again in parables, and said: The kingdom of heaven is made like a man, a king,
who held a wedding feast for his son, and sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, and they would not come.
Again he sent other servants, and said: Tell those who are invited: Behold, my bulls and the fatlings are slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the wedding feast.
But they paid no heed and went away, one to his village, another to his trade. And some others seized his servants, insulted them, and killed them.
Then the king, when he heard it, became angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
Then he said to his servants: The wedding feast is indeed ready, but those who were invited were not worthy of it. Go out, then, into the [?]
that is poured out on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you slew [?] between the [?]. Truly I say to you,
the eagles gather together. Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light,
and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven.
And then all the peoples of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and might. And he will send
his angels with trumpets and a great voice, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds and from the heights of the heavens
to their bounds. Learn a parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves,
you know that summer is near. So also, when you see all this, know that it is near you, at the very doors. Truly I
say to you that this generation will not pass away before all this happens. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
[took their] lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride. Five of them were foolish and five were wise. The five foolish ones
took lamps with them but took no oil with them. The wise ones, however, took oil with their lamps. But while the bridegroom was delaying,
they all grew drowsy and slept. In the night a cry went up: "See, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him."
Then all the virgins rose and [?] their lamps. The foolish ones said to the wise: "Give us some of your oil,
because our lamps are going out." The wise ones answered, saying: "In case there is not enough for us and for you, go instead
to those who sell it and buy some for yourselves." While they were going to buy it, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready went in
with him to the wedding, and the door was shut. At last the other virgins come, saying: "Lord,
Lord, open to us." And he answers and says: "Truly I say to you, I do not know you." Therefore [?] such [?]
because you know neither [?] nor the hour. [A man] who was going abroad called his servants and handed over his goods to them
which is prepared for the devil and his angels. I was hungry and you gave me no food; [?] you gave me no [?]; I was a stranger and you did not take me in;
naked, and you did not clothe me; I was sick [?] and you did not visit me." Then they will answer, saying: "Lord, when
did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not serve you?"
Then he will answer them, saying: "Truly I say to you, as long as you did not do it for one of the least of mine, you did not do it for me either."
And then they will go into the eternal torment of death, but the righteous into eternal life. And it happened, when Jesus had finished all these words that he had spoken,
